summary: Task 03 is implemented exactly as specified: both fields are added to the model with correct semantics, DEFAULT_DATA.version is the only version literal bumped, the historical `version < 7` block is byte-identical, the new `version < 8` block follows the existing style, and the sanitization block sits outside every version branch so already-migrated damaged data is repaired on load. Both sanitizers take `unknown`, are pure, never throw, and every aliasing hazard the task called out (createDefaultBoard, per-board arrays, both early returns) is handled and covered by a test. Verified independently: `npx vitest run tests/unit/migration.test.ts` = 32 passed, `npm test` = 79 passed / 6 files, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `cleanupOrphanedTasks` still derives live ids from `Object.values(board.groups)`. Only minor, optional findings remain.

suggestions.suggestion: `makeGroup(): Group` (line 12) and `makeBoard(): Board` (line 23) still return literals without the newly required `title` / `groupOrder`. The annotations no longer match the interfaces; this stays invisible only because `tsconfig.json` has `"include": ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.svelte"]`, so `tests/` is never type-checked, and vitest does not type-check either. Add `title: ''` to `makeGroup` and `groupOrder: [...GROUP_IDS]` to `makeBoard` (GROUP_IDS is already imported in that file). No runtime impact — `cleanup.ts` touches neither field — and the suite is green today.
suggestions.benefit: Fixtures stay structurally valid against the model, so the day tests are added to the type-check gate (or a `Board`-shaped fixture is reused by a feature that does read `groupOrder`) there is no surprise batch of errors to untangle.

suggestions.suggestion: The two early returns (lines 47-54 and 59-66) are now byte-identical four-line object literals preceded by an identical two-line comment. A single local helper — e.g. `function freshDefaultData(): PluginData { return { ...DEFAULT_DATA, boards: [{ ...DEFAULT_DATA.boards[0], groupOrder: [...DEFAULT_DATA.boards[0].groupOrder] }] }; }` called from both — keeps the comment in one place and removes the risk that a future field is copied into one branch only. This was a single duplicated line before the change, so the duplication is newly meaningful rather than pre-existing noise.
suggestions.benefit: One place to update when the next required field is added; the two paths cannot drift apart silently.

suggestions.suggestion: `value.trim().slice(0, GROUP_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH)` cuts on UTF-16 code units, so a stored title whose 40th and 41st units form a surrogate pair (any non-BMP emoji) is truncated to a lone surrogate that renders as a replacement character and round-trips into `data.json` that way. The input field of Task 8 cannot produce this — `maxlength` also counts code units but the browser refuses to split a pair — so it is reachable only through hand-edited files, which is exactly this sanitizer's audience. If you want it exact: `[...value.trim()].slice(0, GROUP_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH).join('')`. Leaving it as is is a defensible read of the spec ("at most 40 characters", same counting rule as the input attribute) — flagging so the choice is deliberate.
suggestions.benefit: A hand-edited emoji title degrades to a shorter valid string instead of a broken glyph persisted back to disk.

suggestions.suggestion: Raising the item the task anticipated (step 7, scope note), for the decisions log only — no change requested here. The shallow spread in both early returns shares more than `groups` and `hiddenGroups`: `settings` and `tasks` are also the module-level `DEFAULT_DATA` instances, so two `migrateData(null)` calls hand back the same `settings` object and the same `tasks` dictionary that `DEFAULT_DATA` owns. All of it is pre-existing behaviour that this commit correctly did not touch (only `groupOrder`, which is new, was given a fresh copy). Worth one line in the decisions log so the wider aliasing is on record rather than rediscovered later.
suggestions.benefit: The known-but-untreated aliasing is documented instead of being re-derived by the next person who reads this function.
